sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: festival logistics planner: confirm a condition-bound pilot

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the venue grid and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The supplier pack review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can confirm a stallholder area when the footprint and power needs are supplied.
Are early bookings always risky?
No, not if the site requirements and operating limits are known.
Someone new shadowed me in the planning shed this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the event season into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The night-market proposal identifies a waterfront zone and interested vendors, but it has no final crowd-flow drawing or wet-weather arrangement.
What cannot be committed from that?
The full vendor capacity and the operating plan if access narrows in rain.
A food court extension last year was straightforward after the vendor list included equipment loads.
What allowed you to confirm it?
The layout and power calculations were completed before contracts went out.
I archived last cycle's notes on the supplier pack and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The festival reserve includes funds for a temporary route study and one evening of stewarding.
Does that fund an entire night market?
No, it funds testing the route and running a limited pilot.
A vendor call about the venue grid ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the planning shed checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the event season.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the supplier pack records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The waterfront authority agreed to a one-evening pilot, provided the route study is completed and the vendor area stays within the marked zone.
What can you commit to?
A limited pilot with those conditions, rather than a season-long market.
I sketched next week's plan for the event season before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the venue grid updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The printed programme closes next month.
Can the pilot appear there?
Yes, as a one-evening trial with its conditions stated.
I compared two options for the supplier pack tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the planning shed handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I confirm a one-evening waterfront night-market pilot?
